findings: - downscale_50 (50% of width and height): accuracy 50.0% (unmodified 92.1%); FPR 73.1%, FNR 19.7% - more genuine pages flagged and more edits missed.
- down_up_50 (50% then back to full size): accuracy 54.9% (unmodified 92.1%); FPR 57.0%, FNR 29.6% - more genuine pages flagged and more edits missed.
- rotate_180 (rotated 180 degrees): accuracy 64.0% (unmodified 92.1%); FPR 61.3%, FNR 2.8% - more genuine pages flagged.
- skew_3deg (rotated 3 degrees (white fill)): accuracy 70.1% (unmodified 92.1%); FPR 28.0%, FNR 32.4% - more genuine pages flagged and more edits missed.
- Mean accuracy by category: re-save 73.2%, low resolution 60.0%, rotation 72.3%, cropping 83.7%, blur 84.8%.
recommendations: - Treat the reported accuracy as valid for clean, upright, full-page PNG/PDF renders only. Variants below lose more than 10 points: jpeg_q85, downscale_75, downscale_50, down_up_50, rotate_90, rotate_180, skew_1deg, skew_3deg, crop_2px.

- Add these degradations to the training copies (rotation by 90/180 and small skew, border crops, downscaling, light blur) for both classes, as was done for JPEG / resize / brightness in v2, and measure the effect by grouped cross-validation on training data before touching a new holdout set.
- Normalise before analysis: deskew and auto-rotate (text-line orientation), trim scanner borders, and resample to a fixed resolution, so the features see a canonical page.
- Make the features scale-aware: tile size and region thresholds are in pixels, so the same edit covers fewer tiles on a downscaled page. Express them relative to page size or text height.
- Reject or flag inputs outside the validated range (very small pages, rotated pages) instead of scoring them silently; the API currently returns a score for every decodable page.
- Re-run this script on every model change; the frozen TEST and HOLDOUT documents are reused here for measurement only, never for training or selection.
